clips.send: Common mix-up: Waves do not carry the medium along with them. A floating ball bobs up and down as a ripple passes; it is not swept away.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Waves do not carry the medium along with them. A floating ball bobs up and down as a ripple passes; it is not swept away.

clips.send: Trough. Lowest point of a transverse wave. The trough is the lowest point below the rest position. A trough is exactly half a wavelength away from a crest. Crests and troughs exist only in transverse waves. Longitudinal waves have compressions and rarefactions instead.
clips.text: Trough. Lowest point of a transverse wave. The trough is the lowest point below the rest position.. A trough is exactly half a wavelength away from a crest.. Crests and troughs exist only in transverse waves. Longitudinal waves have compressions and rarefactions instead.

clips.send: Rest position. Where the medium sits with no wave. The rest (equilibrium) position is where the rope would be if no wave were passing. Amplitude is measured from this line. Each part of the medium vibrates around its rest position and always comes back to it.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Higher frequency does not mean faster. In the same medium the speed stays the same — the waves just get shorter.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Higher frequency does not mean faster. In the same medium the speed stays the same — the waves just get shorter.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Amplitude is NOT the height from trough to crest. That distance is two amplitudes.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Amplitude is NOT the height from trough to crest. That distance is two amplitudes.

clips.send: Amplitude. How big the vibration is. Amplitude is the distance from the rest position to a crest (or to a trough). Bigger amplitude equals more energy. The energy grows with the amplitude squared: double A, 4 times the energy. For sound, larger amplitude means louder; for light, brighter; for water, taller waves.
clips.text: Amplitude. How big the vibration is. Amplitude is the distance from the rest position to a crest (or to a trough).. Bigger amplitude = more energy. The energy grows with the amplitude squared: double A → 4× the energy.. For sound, larger amplitude means louder; for light, brighter; for water, taller waves.

clips.send: The medium (red bead). What the wave travels through. The rope, the slinky, water and air are all media (plural of medium). Follow the red bead: it only moves up and down (or back and forth) around its rest position, then returns. The ENERGY travels along the wave. The medium itself stays in place.

clips.send: Compression. Where the coils are squeezed together. In a longitudinal wave the medium vibrates back and forth, parallel to the direction the wave travels. A compression is a region where the particles (or coils) are crowded close together. Sound is a longitudinal wave: compressions in air are regions of slightly higher pressure.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A surfer being pushed to shore does not mean waves carry water along. Out in open water, the water mostly moves in small circles in place — it is the energy that travels forward.
clips.text: Common mix-up: A surfer being pushed to shore does not mean waves carry water along. Out in open water, the water mostly moves in small circles in place — it is the energy that travels forward.

clips.send: Rarefaction. Where the coils are spread apart. A rarefaction is a region where the particles are spread out. Compressions and rarefactions alternate along a longitudinal wave. The wavelength of a longitudinal wave is the distance from one compression to the next.
clips.text: Rarefaction. Where the coils are spread apart. A rarefaction is a region where the particles are spread out.. Compressions and rarefactions alternate along a longitudinal wave.. The wavelength of a longitudinal wave is the distance from one compression to the next.

clips.send: Common mix-up: In a longitudinal wave nothing goes up and down — the coils move back and forth along the slinky.
clips.text: Common mix-up: In a longitudinal wave nothing goes up and down — the coils move back and forth along the slinky.

clips.send: Vibrating source (frequency). Where every wave begins. Every wave starts with a vibration: a hand shaking a rope, a speaker cone, a pebble dropped in a pond. Frequency (f) is the number of complete waves made — or passing a point — each second. Unit: hertz (Hz). 1 Hz equals 1 wave per second. Period T equals 1 divided by f is the time for one complete wave. Wave speed v equals f times λ.

Frequency (f) is the number of complete waves made — or passing a point — each second. Unit: hertz (Hz). 1 Hz = 1 wave per second.. Period T = 1 ÷ f is the time for one complete wave. Wave speed v = f × λ.

clips.send: Crest. Highest point of a transverse wave. The crest is the highest point above the rest position. In a transverse wave the medium moves at right angles (perpendicular) to the direction the wave travels. The distance from one crest to the next is one wavelength.
clips.text: Crest. Highest point of a transverse wave. The crest is the highest point above the rest position.. In a transverse wave the medium moves at right angles (perpendicular) to the direction the wave travels.. The distance from one crest to the next is one wavelength.

clips.send: Wavelength (λ). Length of one complete wave. Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next crest (or trough to trough, or compression to compression). Its symbol is the Greek letter λ (lambda), measured in metres. In the same medium, higher frequency means shorter wavelength, because v equals f times λ stays the same.
clips.text: Wavelength (λ). Length of one complete wave. Wavelength is the distance from one crest to the next crest (or trough to trough, or compression to compression).. Its symbol is the Greek letter λ (lambda), measured in metres.. In the same medium, higher frequency means shorter wavelength, because v = f × λ stays the same.

clips.send: 波谷。横波的最低点。波谷是低于平衡位置最多的点。波谷与相邻的波峰恰好相距半个波长。只有横波才有波峰和波谷，纵波对应的是密部和疏部。
clips.text: 波谷. 横波的最低点. 波谷是低于平衡位置最多的点。. 波谷与相邻的波峰恰好相距半个波长。. 只有横波才有波峰和波谷，纵波对应的是密部和疏部。

clips.send: 平衡位置。没有波时介质所在的位置。平衡位置是没有波经过时绳子所在的位置。振幅就是从这条线开始测量的。介质的每一部分都在平衡位置附近振动，并且总会回到这里。

clips.send: 容易混淆：频率高并不代表波速快。在同一种介质中波速不变，只是波长变短了。
clips.text: 容易混淆：频率高并不代表波速快。在同一种介质中波速不变，只是波长变短了。

clips.send: 振幅。振动的幅度。振幅是从平衡位置到波峰（或波谷）的距离。振幅越大，波携带的能量越多。能量与振幅的平方成正比：振幅变为 2 倍，能量变为 4 倍。对声音来说，振幅越大响度越大；对光来说越亮；对水波来说浪越高。
clips.text: 振幅. 振动的幅度. 振幅是从平衡位置到波峰（或波谷）的距离。. 振幅越大，波携带的能量越多。能量与振幅的平方成正比：振幅变为 2 倍，能量变为 4 倍。. 对声音来说，振幅越大响度越大；对光来说越亮；对水波来说浪越高。

clips.send: 容易混淆：振幅不是从波谷到波峰的高度，那是振幅的 2 倍。

clips.send: 介质（红色小球）。波传播所经过的物质。绳子、弹簧、水和空气都是介质。盯住红色小球：它只是在平衡位置附近上下（或前后）振动，然后回到原处。沿着波前进的是能量，介质本身留在原地。
clips.text: 介质（红色小球）. 波传播所经过的物质. 绳子、弹簧、水和空气都是介质。. 盯住红色小球：它只是在平衡位置附近上下（或前后）振动，然后回到原处。. 沿着波前进的是能量，介质本身留在原地。

clips.send: 波峰。横波的最高点。波峰是高出平衡位置最多的点。在横波中，介质的振动方向与波的传播方向垂直。相邻两个波峰之间的距离就是一个波长。
clips.text: 波峰. 横波的最高点. 波峰是高出平衡位置最多的点。. 在横波中，介质的振动方向与波的传播方向垂直。. 相邻两个波峰之间的距离就是一个波长。

clips.send: 容易混淆：纵波中没有东西上下运动，弹簧圈是沿着弹簧前后移动的。
clips.text: 容易混淆：纵波中没有东西上下运动，弹簧圈是沿着弹簧前后移动的。

clips.send: 密部。弹簧圈被挤紧的地方。在纵波中，介质沿着波的传播方向前后振动（两者方向平行）。密部是粒子（或弹簧圈）挤在一起的区域。声波是纵波：空气中的密部就是压强稍高的区域。
clips.text: 密部. 弹簧圈被挤紧的地方. 在纵波中，介质沿着波的传播方向前后振动（两者方向平行）。. 密部是粒子（或弹簧圈）挤在一起的区域。. 声波是纵波：空气中的密部就是压强稍高的区域。

clips.send: 疏部。弹簧圈被拉开的地方。疏部是粒子分散开的区域。在纵波中，密部和疏部交替出现。纵波的波长是相邻两个密部之间的距离。
clips.text: 疏部. 弹簧圈被拉开的地方. 疏部是粒子分散开的区域。. 在纵波中，密部和疏部交替出现。. 纵波的波长是相邻两个密部之间的距离。

clips.send: 波源（频率）。所有的波都从振动开始。所有的波都从振动开始：抖动绳子的手、扬声器的纸盆、落入池塘的石子。频率，f， 是每秒产生（或经过某一点）的完整波的个数，单位是赫兹，Hz。1 Hz 表示每秒 1 个波。周期 T 等于 1 除以 f，是完成一个完整波所需的时间。波速 v 等于 f 乘 λ。
clips.text: 波源（频率）. 所有的波都从振动开始. 所有的波都从振动开始：抖动绳子的手、扬声器的纸盆、落入池塘的石子。. 频率（f） 是每秒产生（或经过某一点）的完整波的个数，单位是赫兹（Hz）。1 Hz 表示每秒 1 个波。. 周期 T = 1 ÷ f，是完成一个完整波所需的时间。波速 v = f × λ。

clips.send: 波长（λ）。一个完整波的长度。波长是相邻两个波峰（或两个波谷、两个密部）之间的距离。波长的符号是希腊字母 λ（读作“兰姆达”），单位是米。在同一种介质中，频率越高，波长越短，因为 v 等于 f 乘 λ 保持不变。
